subject: mirtCAT simulation using the MSD model

messages.author: 6855b04443295af7
messages.subject: mirtCAT simulation using the MSD model
parts:
Hi Phil, 

I hope this message finds you well. 

I wonder if it is possible to conduct a CAT simulation using the method of successive dichotomizations (MSD) model in the mirtCAT package?  

I've been able to calculate the parameters using the msd R package, but it would be even better if I could do it using the mirt package. I know I could technically split the polytomous data and then run multiple 2PL models, but I'm not sure what it would entail for cat simulations. 

I know it would involve customisation but I am not entirely sure how I could do that. 
It would be great if you could provide a snippet of code for me to figure things out. 

Kind regards,
Aiden

Bradley, C., & Massof, R. W. (2018). Method of successive dichotomizations: an improved method for estimating measures of latent variables from rating scale data. PloS one, 13(10), e0206106.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT simulation using the MSD model
parts:
Hi Aiden,

I'm fairly certain this is just the graded rating scale model ('grsm') that's already in the mirt package, where the slope parameters are fixed to 1 to further anchor the scale and VAR(theta) is estimated instead (much the same as Rasch models). Hence, mirtCAT should already support this model, though you'll need to translate the constrained graded rating scale model into the standard GRM model by distributing the item shift parameter into each of the estimated intercept terms while also including the VAR(theta) term in mirtCAT() to account of this variance shift (otherwise, you can rescale the slopes to match this as well... it makes no difference). HTH.

Phil

Hi Phil, 

I missed your reply. So sorry about that. Thank you for your reply. 
I tried to code it, but I can't seem to get it right. Mmm. 
If I look at the coefficients, the a1 parameter isn't fixed to 1. I tried to use mod2values() and fix the a1 parameter to 1, but I encountered an error. Even if I did not change the a1 values and ran mirt(Science, model = 1, pars = pars), I still received the same error. 

# Fit the initial GRSM model
model_grsm <- mirt(Science, 1, itemtype = "grsm")

> coef(model_grsm, simplify=TRUE)
$items
                     a1        b1       b2        b3      c
Comfort   1.718 3.549 1.683 -0.955  0.000
Work         1.117 3.549 1.683 -0.955 -0.947
Future       1.245 3.549 1.683 -0.955 -0.294
Benefit      1.114 3.549 1.683 -0.955 -0.683

# Extract the parameters
pars <- mod2values(model_grsm)
pars

# Modify the parameter values to fix a1 to 1
pars$value[pars$name == "a1"] <- 1  # Fix slopes to 1
values$est[values$name == "a1"] <- FALSE  

# Refit the model with the modified parameters [ERROR]
fixed_model <- mirt(Science, model = 1, pars = pars)

Error: Rows in supplied and starting value data.frame objects do not match. Were the
             data or itemtype input arguments modified?

============================================================

Assuming once I get the parameters from the fixed model, how should I translate the constrained GRSM into the standard GRM in mirtCAT()?
Something like the below?

# extract coefficients
params_grsm =coef(fixed_model, simplify=TRUE)

# Adjust the b values by distributing the shift parameter c
params_grm <- params_grsm$items  

# For each item, adjust the b values
for (i in 1:nrow(params_grm)) {
  params_grm[i, "b1"] <- params_grm[i, "b1"] - params_grm[i, "c"]
  params_grm[i, "b2"] <- params_grm[i, "b2"] - params_grm[i, "c"]
  params_grm[i, "b3"] <- params_grm[i, "b3"] - params_grm[i, "c"]
}

# Remove the shift parameter c from the model (as it is now incorporated into the b values)
params_grm <- params_grm[, !colnames(params_grm) %in% "c"]
print(params_grm)

# Estimate the theta scores for all respondents
theta_scores <- fscores(fixed_model)

# Calculate the variance of the theta scores
VAR_theta <- var(theta_scores)

# Adjust thresholds by incorporating VAR(theta)
thresholds <- grep("^b", colnames(params_grm))
params_grm[, thresholds] <- params_grm[, thresholds] * as.vector(sqrt(VAR_theta))

# Create mirtCAT object with adjusted itempool and theta prior
# Where can i include VAR(theta) in the mirtCAT function? I've rescaled the slopes by incorporating VAR(theta) above, so maybe I don't have to do this step anymore? 
mirtCAT_object <- mirtCAT(mo = itempool, 
                          model = rep("graded", nrow(itempool)),
                          method = "MAP",
                          criteria = "MEPV",
                          theta_range = c(-6, 6))


Thanks for your help! 
Aiden

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirtCAT simulation using the MSD model
parts:
Hi Aiden,

Yes, you should reduce to a model that mirtCAT currently supports. Much of the CAT computations are done at the C++ level to evaluate the test bank properties, which for large banks is non-trivial to do quickly, which is why customized item types and other specialized IRT models are not currently supported. Sorry if this is annoying ....

Phil
